title: A kinetic-impact deflection model
target: Estimate a velocity change and explain the value of lead time.
criteria: Connect delivered momentum to target velocity change.
Explain why real deflection includes ejecta and orbital effects.

authoring.limitations: Reasoning evidence only. Multiple choice does not certify physical performance. Teacher reviews before assigning and rates mastery separately.

cpa.prompt: A simplified kinetic-impact model treats a small probe as sticking to a target with negligible external impulse during impact. Which equation governs their shared final velocity?
options: Momentum is ignored because the target is large.
Final velocity = probe mass alone.
Every impact conserves kinetic energy.
Total initial momentum = combined mass × final velocity.
cpa.guide: Use a perfectly inelastic momentum balance over the brief collision.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

cpa.prompt: What does a straight-line drift estimate Δx = Δv × t assume after a brief sideways push?
options: The target instantly travels the full offset.
The added sideways velocity stays approximately constant over the modeled interval.
A continued sideways acceleration of Δv occurs every second.
The velocity change is measured in meters.
cpa.guide: The equation models constant added velocity after the impulse.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

cpa.prompt: A 2,000 kg target receives a sideways impulse of 10 N·s. What is its sideways velocity change?
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: An added sideways velocity of 0.03 m/s persists for 400 s in a drift model. What offset results?
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: Why can real impact momentum transfer differ from a simple sticking model?
options: Impulse exists only in air.
Momentum has no direction in space.
Ejected material can carry momentum away.
Target mass never matters.
cpa.guide: Ejecta must be included in the full system momentum account.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Compare evidence and identify a physical relationship.

cpa.prompt: A long-term orbital deflection is predicted using only a straight-line offset. What limitation should be stated?
options: The simple formula predicts exact ground damage.
A small velocity change cannot accumulate any offset.
Gravity and orbital geometry can alter how the initial velocity change develops.
Long-term gravity is always exactly zero.
cpa.guide: The drift approximation is useful over limited conditions but not a full orbital forecast.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Select a claim supported by the stated evidence and assumptions.
